subject: Service fencing evidence and topology request - Redwood Dedicated/Private
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@edencloud.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-25T08:12:00Z
Subject: Evidence request: isolation & service fencing for Dedicated/Private environments

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this — EdenCloud's compliance team has a tight SIG questionnaire due next week. They specifically asked for a concise narrative and diagram showing how Redwood enforces "service-level fencing" between customer Dedicated pools and Private deployments (control plane boundaries, network egress controls, and KMS/domain-of-control for customer keys).

Can you provide: 
- One-page narrative we can paste into the SIG response (high-level, 3–4 bullets).
- A single network diagram (PDF/PNG) that shows the control plane vs data plane, tenant compute overlay, and egress chokepoints.
- A short CSV index of artifact evidence we can attach (SOC 2 reports, runbooks, and config export pointers).

If you already have an internal template, that would be ideal — we just need something Eden's auditor can hand to their reviewer. 

Appreciate quick turnaround — deadline is 2027-05-31.

Best,
Sam
Sam Jenkins
Security Program Manager, EdenCloud
security@edencloud.com

Attachment: none
From: monica.patel@redwood.ai
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@edencloud.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-25T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: isolation & service fencing for Dedicated/Private environments

Sam — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a short packet that should meet the auditor's immediate needs. Contents attached below:

- service-fencing-topology.pdf: single-page network diagram (control plane vs data plane, tenant compute overlay, ingress/egress points, firewall zones).
- ctlplane-seg_v2.png: simplified control-plane isolation zoom for SOC reviewers.
- soc2-evidence-index.csv: pointer file listing SOC 2 report, versions, runbook IDs, and configuration exports with timestamps.

Quick three-bullet narrative you can use in the SIG response: 
1) Redwood separates control plane (multi-tenant, managed by Redwood) from customer data plane (Dedicated and Private) through strict network ACLs and tenant tagging at the orchestration and runtime layers — control-plane operations require RBAC and mTLS to reach any node.
2) Data plane instances for Dedicated/Private are deployed into customer-dedicated subnets or customer VPCs; egress is routed through managed egress gateways with enforced egress ACLs and DLP hooks.
3) Customer encryption keys are optionally customer-managed (KMS/HSM) and never persist in Redwood control-plane logs; key usage is audited and recorded to immutable audit streams retained per contract.

Notes & next steps: 
- The diagram highlights the default deployment; we can produce a variant showing air-gapped on-prem placement if Eden needs it.
- Marcus, can you validate the KMS/egress wording (esp. the claim about no key persistence in control-plane logs)?
- Kimberly, flag any items that should go into the CSV index before I send to Sam.

Thanks — sending now as requested to meet your 5/31 cutoff.

--
Monica Patel
Manager, Solutions Security
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Evidence request: isolation & service fencing for Dedicated/Private environments

Monica — quick clarifications for Eden: 

- KMS boundary: we support both Redwood-managed keys (default) and customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/Azure KeyVault/GCP Cloud KMS and on-prem HSM. When customer-managed keys are used, Redwood holds no plaintext key material; operations use an encrypt/decrypt call pattern and we only store key reference IDs. I'll add a single sentence to the narrative to make that explicit.
- Egress chokepoints: we enforce egress via managed gateways and can provide firewall rule sets (CIDR/port lists) per tenant. If Eden needs packet captures or flow logs, we can provide 7 days of flow logs by default and up to 90 days as an add-on.

Sam — confirm whether you want the CSV index to include sample firewall ACL exports and a redacted flow log sample; I can include both as separate artifacts.

--
Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@edencloud.com>, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-25T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: isolation & service fencing for Dedicated/Private environments

Sam / Monica — confirming the technical assertions: 

1) Control plane vs data plane: control plane runs in Redwood-managed VPCs with dedicated subnets for control services (auth, scheduler, key manager proxy). Data plane for Dedicated customers is deployed into isolated compute pools with tenant tagging; for Private deployments, the data plane is deployed into customer VPCs or on-prem environments and communicates over mTLS tunnels initiated from the customer-managed overlay.
2) Key handling: when customers opt for CMK (customer-managed keys), Redwood uses a short-lived, per-request token to call the KMS; ciphertext and key references are stored but not private key material. Audit records for key operations are sent to our immutable audit stream (write-once storage) and are included in the SOC 2 evidence bundle.
3) Egress & enforcement: egress is funneled through managed egress gateways with a policy engine that enforces allowlists, header stripping for PII, and optional DLP engine inspection. For Dedicated customers we can enable per-tenant egress NAT to provide distinguishable egress IPs.

Artifact checklist (matching attached CSV): 
- SOC2_report_2026_v3.pdf (redacted) — available on request via secure link
- service-fencing-topology.pdf (attached)
- ctlplane-seg_v2.png (attached)
- firewall-acl-export-redacted.csv (optional)
- redacted-flow-sample-20270501.pcap (optional, request by May 28)

Sam — I recommend including the two attached images in the SIG packet and referencing the SOC 2 PDF via a secure link (we can generate a short-lived URL and add it to the CSV). Monica + Kimberly — happy to field any technical follow-ups from Eden's auditor tomorrow morning (PT).

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
